newsitem.title: CANADA: Teck hedged against gold price fall.
newsitem.headline: Teck hedged against gold price fall.

text.p: Canadian miner Teck Corp said on Thursday that its gold hedging program would help protect it from the recent drop in gold prices.

Teck, which produced 164,000 ounces of gold in the first half, said it had hedge contracts covering 325,000 ounces of gold at an average sales price of US$407. The spot price of gold recently dropped below US$320 an ounce.

"The company's gold hedging program has secured price protection on 325,000 ounces of gold production at an average price of US$407 per ounce, of which contracts for 217,000 ounces are realizable over the next 24 months," Teck said.

Teck earlier reported earnings of C$0.16 a share for the second quarter, down from C$0.20 a year ago. In the second quarter, it realized an average price for gold of US$361 an ounce, down from US$397 a year earlier.
Gold production, principally from its Hemlo operations, was 77,000 ounces in the second quarter. Its six-month gold production was 164,000 ounces, compared with 174,000 ounces a year ago.

Teck said the lower production was due to lower grade ores being processed at the two Hemlo mines in the second quarter. But it said the mines were expected to achieve forecast production for the year of 330,000 ounces.

Cash operating costs at the Hemlo mines averaged US$245 per ounce in the second quarter and US$229 per ounce in the first six months. The second-quarter average realized gold price was US$361 an ounce compared with US$397 in 1996.
Teck said it had a strong balance sheet.
At June 30, its working capital was C$351 million. Cash net of short-term bank loans was C$281 million compared with C$346 million at the beginning of the second quarter.
Long-term debt, excluding convertible and exchangeable debentures, was C$227 million, or nine percent of total capitalization.
